title: Canonicalize late-event rollups and quota attribution for Console analytics
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Summary:
Console per-model usage charts and the billing ledger diverge when events arrive late or are re-emitted by upstream systems (retries, retries+dedupe, and cross-region replication). We currently surface a timeseries based on first-pass rollups which causes transient undercounts followed by large backfills in the Console charts and occasional double-counting in quota reconciliation.

Root cause hypotheses validated by spike:
- Ingestion pipeline treats ingestion time as the canonical time instead of event time, so late events land in past buckets but are aggregated into the current rollup snapshot.
- The rollup job is not idempotent for replays; duplicate event ids lead to over-counting when backfills occur.
- Rate-limiter/quota accounting uses different aggregation windows and relies on different sources (real-time limiter vs. batched rollups), producing attribution mismatches per model and per-customer.

Proposed plan (high level):
1) Introduce an event-time-aware canonicalizer in the rollup pipeline that dedupes by request_id + model_version and assigns a stable watermark to each aggregation bucket. Use compacted Kafka topic for canonicalized events.
2) Make hourly/daily rollups idempotent by storing last-applied-event-id per (customer,model,window) and skipping re-applies.
3) Add a short-lived 'pending' bucket for late-arriving events and expose how many tokens are pending backfill in the Console so customers see expected revisions.
4) Reconcile rate-limiter logs and billing ledger by running a nightly join job that computes any offset corrections and emits correction records that the Console can apply atomically to timeseries.
5) Add monitoring and alerting: drift >1% between ledger and console triggers automated investigation runbook.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strong consistency vs. user-visible latency: we prefer eventual correctness with transparent pending indicators rather than blocking writes or increasing customer-perceived latency.
- Storage and state complexity: per-window last-applied-event-id increases state, but reduces re-aggregation cost on backfills.

Rollout notes:
- Start with a small cohort (internal tenants + alpha customers) for 7 days.
- Run backfill in dry-run mode for 48 hours and compare corrections.
- Gradually enable idempotent apply and canonicalized feed for all customers after Q/A and metrics pass.
acceptance_criteria: Per-model Console charts and billing ledger drift <= 1% for the last 90 days after backfills are applied
Backfill pipeline is idempotent: reprocessing the same events does not change final aggregated tokens
Console displays pending-backfill counts for any window with late events
Nightly reconciliation job emits correction records and the Console applies them without duplicate credits/debits
QA runbook executed and verified on alpha cohort: PRD signoff from billing PM and Console PM
